title: Count every track the home screen prefetches

blocks.text: The music app shows a banner above the playlists on its home screen while it prefetches their tracks: "3 tracks from @tobi, @mira". Users with long playlists see a banner that counts far too few tracks, and since a few accounts were deleted, some banners read "@null".
`Prefetch.banner(...)` already builds the text. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Prefetch.java`:

items: `trackCount(...)`: how many tracks the player fetches across all the playlists;
`ownerHandles(...)`: the owners' handles, each once, in the order of their first playlist, and nothing at all for an owner whose account is gone.

blocks.text: `Profiles.handleOf(...)` answers with an empty `Optional` for a deleted account. About four lines in total.

cases.says: for playlists of one track each by known owners, the banner counts the tracks and names each owner once, in playlist order
no playlists means no tracks and no owners
the count is of tracks across all playlists, including a playlist with none, not of playlists
an owner with no handle contributes nothing to the list of handles, not a null

origin.section: map Gives One Result per Element; flatMap Splices a Stream per Element into One

concepts: map passes on one result per element, so mapping to a list gives a stream of lists; flatMap passes on the elements of the stream each element maps to, zero or more.
flatMap(Optional::stream) keeps the values of present Optionals and drops the empty ones, where unwrapping with orElse(null) leaves nulls in the stream.
